macro.reasoning: The temperature series shows a clear seasonal warming trend from late June (~29°C) to early August (~32°C), followed by a sharp drop to 29.2°C on Aug 10 associated with a wet, humid spell (8.6 mm rain, 71% humidity). The last 10 days display high volatility (29–32.6°C) driven by alternating dry/windy and wet/humid regimes. With no further exogenous forecasts, the most defensible assumption is a continuation of the underlying summer warming trend moderated by the recent cool, wet perturbation. A simple damped-trend extrapolation from the last 14-day linear fit (≈ +0.04 °C/day) anchored at the last observation (29.2°C) yields a gradual recovery toward the early-August mean (~31.5°C) over the 7-day horizon, giving the predicted sequence above.

micro.reasoning: Temperature dropped sharply to 29.2°C with high humidity (71%) and moderate rain (8.6mm) on Aug 10, breaking the recent hot/dry pattern. Historical analogs show post-rain rebounds of 0.5-1.5°C/day as humidity falls. Forecast assumes gradual clearing and warming toward the 31-32°C range seen in late July/early August.
step_reasoning: Day 1: Post-rain clearing begins; humidity drops from 71% toward 60s, temp rises ~0.3°C to 29.5°C.
Day 2: Continued drying, wind lightens; temp climbs ~0.5°C to 30.0°C.
Day 3: Pattern resembles July 27-28 rebound; another ~0.5°C rise to 30.5°C.
Day 4: Approaching the 31°C level seen in late July; +0.5°C to 31.0°C.
Day 5: Reaches 31.5°C, matching the plateau observed July 31-Aug 6.
Day 6: Stabilizes near 31.5°C as hot/dry regime re-establishes.
Day 7: Holds at 31.5°C consistent with recent summer peak temperatures.

synthesis.reasoning: Combined macro (damped trend +0.04°C/day from 29.2°C) and micro (post-rain rebound analog) forecasts with 50/50 weight. Both agree on gradual warming from the Aug 10 cool/wet anomaly (29.2°C) toward the early-August mean (~31.5°C). Macro projects a steady linear recovery; micro expects faster initial rebound then plateau. The blended path splits the difference: ~0.3-0.45°C/day for the first four days, then slowing to ~0.1°C/day as the seasonal peak is approached. Uncertainty remains elevated (±1°C) due to regime-switching volatility seen in the last 10 days.
